title: Relative scalar-quotient presentation of PGL2 and its triangular subgroups
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $G,B,D$ be group schemes over $S$ [def-sc-group-scheme], with group homomorphisms $i_B:B\to G$ and $i_D:D\to B$. For an $S$-scheme $V$, put $Q(V)=\operatorname{GL}_2(\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V))/\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)^\times$, where $\operatorname{GL}_2(R)$ is the group of invertible $2\times2$ matrices and units act by scalar matrices. A relative triangular presentation consists of injective group homomorphisms $q_V:Q(V)\to G(V)$, natural for entrywise pullback along every $S$-morphism, such that every $G$-section fppf locally lifts to an invertible matrix. Here fppf locally [def-pc-fppf-site] means there is a covering sieve $R$ on $V$ such that the assertion holds after every $h:W\to V$ in $R$. The maps $i_B,i_D$ are closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. A section $z\in G(V)$ is in the image of $B(V)$ if and only if fppf locally $z|_W=q_W([m])$ with $m_{10}=0$; it is in the image of $D(V)$ under $i_B i_D$ if and only if fppf locally it has such a lift with both $m_{10}=m_{01}=0$. Thus these are exactly the represented fppf scalar quotient and its upper triangular and diagonal subgroup sheaf images, over arbitrary bases and with no assumption of global matrix lifts.
